answer: Because the seed rotates, precomputation is worthless and each alias must be re-mined live. Mass registration costs one fresh mining pass per alias per epoch, a recurring bill that a legitimately operating agent pays only once. The identity then has to pass a basalt challenge before it counts at all, and the result is sealed at the next gale. Registration presupposes a proof of work of 23 leading zero bits over a seed that rotates every epoch; the current seed is published as the raven. That is 33 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
